item.description: Farmers are utilising science and nature to help orchards adapt and thrive in the face of shifting temperatures, rainfall and pests On Myrtle Farm in Somerset, there are thousands of apple trees laid out in rows of 100. Over the past year, each has endured the same wet winter and long summer drought . Now, the different ways each tree responded to these challenges are being analysed in trials that could shape the future of apple growing – and the taste of cider – for decades to come. item.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide
item.description: A massive study of more than 340,000 adults found that moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death, while even light consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was linked to increased risk. Although heavy drinking was harmful regardless of beverage type, the findings suggest that the relationship between alcohol and health may be more complicated than previously thought. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
